sanskrit: viśvaṃ vivyajmi pṛthivīva puṣṭam āyadāyat prati gṛhṇāmy annam | vaiśvānarasya mahato mahimnā- -agniṣ ṭad viśvād agadaṃ kṛṇotu ||
english: I encompass all, as the earth encompasses abundance; I receive food as it comes and goes. By the great greatness of Vaiśvānara, may Agni make that wholly free of disease.

sanskrit: yad annam admi bahudhā virūpaṃ hiraṇyam aśvam uta gām ajām avim | vaiśvānarasya (…) ||
english: Whatever food I eat in manifold and varied forms — gold, horse, cow, goat, or sheep — by the great greatness of Vaiśvānara, may Agni make that wholly free of disease.

sanskrit: yad annam admy anṛtena devā dāsyann adāsyann uta vā kariṣyan | vaiśvānarasya (…) ||
english: Whatever food I eat in untruth, O gods — whether I was about to give, or not give, or was about to act — by the great greatness of Vaiśvānara, may Agni make that wholly free of disease.

sanskrit: yan mā hutaṃ yad ahutam ājagāma yasmād annān manasodrārajīmi | vaiśvānarasya mahato mahimnā- -agniṣ ṭad viśvād agadaṃ kṛṇotu ||
english: What has come to me as offered oblation or as unoffered gift, from whatever food my mind shrinks back in repulsion — by the great greatness of Vaiśvānara, may Agni make that wholly free of disease.

sanskrit: jamadagniḥ kaśyapaḥ svādv etad bharadvājo madhv annaṃ kṛṇotu | pratigrahītre gotamo vasiṣṭho viśvāmitro naḥ pra tirāty āyuḥ ||
english: May Jamadagni, Kaśyapa — this is sweet — may Bharadvāja make the food honey-sweet. For the receiver: Gotama, Vasiṣṭha, and Viśvāmitra extend our life onward.

sanskrit: agne yajñasya cakṣo | idaṃ vedāma yathedaṃ bhaviṣyati svāhā ||
english: O Agni, eye of the sacrifice — this we know, as this shall come to be. Svāhā!

sanskrit: agne yajñasya śrotra | idaṃ vedāma yathedaṃ bhaviṣyati svāhā ||
english: O Agni, ear of the sacrifice — this we know, as this shall come to be. Svāhā!

sanskrit: agne yajñasya prāṇa | idaṃ vedāma yathedaṃ bhaviṣyati svāhā ||
english: O Agni, in-breath of the sacrifice — this we know, as this shall come to be. Svāhā!

sanskrit: agne yajñasyāpāna | idaṃ vedāma yathedaṃ bhaviṣyati svāhā ||
english: O Agni, out-breath of the sacrifice — this we know, as this shall come to be. Svāhā!

sanskrit: agne yajñasyātman | idaṃ vedāma yathedaṃ bhaviṣyati svāhā ||
english: O Agni, self of the sacrifice — this we know, as this shall come to be. Svāhā!

sanskrit: agne yajñasya sarva | idaṃ vedāma yathedaṃ bhaviṣyati svāhā ||
english: O Agni, all of the sacrifice — this we know, as this shall come to be. Svāhā!

sanskrit: devānāṃ bhadrā sumatir ṛjūyatāṃ devānāṃ rātir abhi no ni vartatām | devānāṃ sakhyam upa sedimā vayaṃ devā na āyuḥ pra tirantu jīvase ||
english: May the benevolent grace of the gods flow straight toward us; may the bounty of the gods turn back upon us. We have drawn near to the friendship of the gods; may the gods extend our life so that we may live.

sanskrit: tān pūrvayā nividā hūmahe vayaṃ bhagaṃ mitram aditiṃ dakṣam asridham | aryamaṇaṃ varuṇaṃ somam aśvinā sarasvatī naḥ subhagā mayas karat ||
english: We summon them with the ancient laudatory formula: Bhaga, Mitra, Aditi, unfailing Dakṣa, Aryaman, Varuṇa, Soma, the two Aśvins — may the auspicious Sarasvatī grant us bliss.

sanskrit: idaṃ pitṛbhyo namo astv adya ye pūrvāso ye 'parāsaḥ pareyuḥ | ye pārthive rajasy ā niṣattā ye vā nūnaṃ suvṛjanāsu vikṣu ||
english: Let this homage be to the Fathers today — those who have gone before and those who went afterward; those who are settled in the earthly realm of dust, and those who now dwell among well-ordered peoples.

sanskrit: pratyañco agne śaravaḥ patantu kṛtyākṛte ripave martyāya | kravyāde atriṇe mā mīmṛḍaḥ kraviṣṇum ā dhehi nirṛter upasthe ||
english: O Agni, let the arrows fly back upon the sorcerer-maker, the mortal enemy. Show no mercy to the flesh-devouring devourer; place the flesh-hungry one in the lap of Nirṛti.

sanskrit: jyāyasaḥ śaṃsād uta vā kanīyasaḥ sajātaśaṃsād uta jāmiśaṃsāt | anādiṣṭam anyakṛtaṃ yad enas tvaṃ nas tasmāj jātavedo mumugdhi ||
english: From the curse of one greater or of one lesser, from the curse of a clansman or the curse of a kinsman, from whatever sin is uninstructed or done by another — from that, O Jātavedas, release us.
